html.body: Date: 2025-03-04 Remarks Reconsideration of the above-identified application in view of the present Amendment is respectfully requested.Claims 1-15 were pending in the application. By this paper, without acquiescing in the grounds for rejection and for expediting prosecution, claims 1, 4 and 8 have been amended, claims 3 and 6 have been cancelled, and new claims 16-22 have been added. No new matter has been added by the present amendment.ALLOWABLE SUBJECT MATTERAt the outset, Applicant notes the indication on page 6 of the Office Action of the allowability of claims 7 and 10-15, if rewritten in independent form, including all of the limitations of the base claim and any intervening claims, and with respect to claims 10-13, also written to overcome the rejections under 35 U.S.C. §112, as set forth in this Office Action. Applicant thanks the Patent Office for favorable review of these claims.Without acquiescing in the grounds for rejection, and for expediting prosecution, as will be further discussed below, Applicant has i) added new claims 16 and 17 based on original claim 1 and allowable claims 14 and 15, respectively; and ii) added new claims 18-22 to depend from independent claims 16 or 17.Claim Rejections Under 35 U.S.C. $112 Claims 10-12 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b), as being indefinite.Without acquiescing in the Patent Office's grounds of rejection, and solely for the purpose of expediting prosecution, claim 10 has been amended with the 35 U.S.C. § 112 rejections in mind.Accordingly, Applicant submits that the amended claims are definite and respectfully requests withdrawal of the 35 U.S.C. § 112 rejections.Claim Reiections Under 35 U.S.C. .. 102 and 103 Claims 1 and 2 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. §102 as being anticipated by U.S.Patent No. 8,523,106 to Thompson, hereinafter Thompson;claims 1, 3, 6, 8 and 9 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. §102 as being anticipated by U.S. Patent No. 11,319,060 to Cottet, hereinafter Cottet; and claims 4 and 5 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being obvious over Cottet.Applicant respectfully traverses these rejections for at least the following reasons.Amended claim 1 (with emphasis added) is reproduced below:A rotorcraft comprising:a fuselage forming at least one lower lateral fuselage compartment with an opening, wherein the at least one lower lateral fuselage compartment comprises at least a first fitting, a second fitting, and a third fitting; and at least one non-retractable wheel-type landing gear rigidly attached in the at least one lower lateral fuselage compartment and extending at least partly through the opening, wherein the at least one non-retractable wheel-type landing gear comprises:at least one wheel;a shock absorber with a length axis and a circumferential direction, the shock absorber being connected to the at least one wheel and including:a shock absorber tube with a length direction, which comprises in the length direction an open end and an axially opposed closed end; and a shock absorber rod telescopically mounted to the shock absorber tube via the open end;a first fixation provided close to the open end on the shock absorber tube and connected to the first fitting;a second fixation provided close to the closed end on the shock absorber tube and connected to the second fitting;a third fixation provided close to the closed end on the shock absorber tube and connected to the third fitting, wherein the third fixation is spaced apart from the second fixation in the circumferential direction of the shock absorber by a predetermined angle;wherein the second fixation and the third fixation are connected to each other via a supporting axle, and wherein the supporting axle is connected to the second fitting and the third fitting such that the supporting axle forms a main hinge axis; and wherein the first fixation forms a hinge axis that is inclined with respect to the main hinge axis.As will be discussed in more detail below, the cited references not disclose, teach or suggest each and every limitation of these claims.Without acquiescing in the Patent Office's grounds of rejection, and solely for the purpose of expediting prosecution, claim 1 has been amended to include the limitations of claims 3 and 6. At the outset, it is noteworthy that claims 3 and 6 were not rejected in view of Thompson.Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that claim 1 is allowable over Thompson for at least this reason.Furthermore, Thompson describes a nose landing gear arrangement 10 for an aircraft. This arrangement 10 comprises a leg assembly having a side brace arrangement 16, 18 that defines a pivot axis at one end thereof. This arrangement 10 also comprises a landing gear wheel mounting 22 at the other end thereof and two stays 42, 44. Each stay is mounted at one end thereof to the leg assembly and being mountable at the other end thereof to an aircraft. Also, each stay comprises an upper stay part 42a, 44a and a lower stay part 42b, 44b hinged together. The upper stay part 42a, 44a has a cardan joint 48 at its end spaced from the hinge 46 to enable hinged mounting to an aircraft. The lower stay part 426, 446 has another cardan joint 48 at its end spaced from the hinge 46. The cardan joint 48 of the lower stay part 42b, 44b is hinged and mounted to the lower stay part 42b, 44b and to the leg assembly. With Thompson, the leg assembly and stays 42, 44 are arranged so that the stays extend from the leg assembly on opposite sides thereof and the stays 42, 44 fold into a stowed position so that the lower stay parts 42b, 44b are arranged substantially alongside the side brace 16, 18 when the leg assembly is retracted. This is illustrated by Figure 1 of Thompson below:FIG. 1 of Thompson However, Thompson fails to disclose, teach or suggest a second fixation and a third fixation that are connected to each other via a supporting axle, such that the supporting axle is connected to the second fitting and the third fitting in such a manner that the supporting axle forms a main hinge axis.Also, Thompson fails to disclose, teach or suggest a first fixation that forms a hinge axis that is inclined with respect to a main hinge axis.Accordingly, for at least the above reasons, independent claim 1 is patentable over Thompson.Cottet describes an aircraft 100 with a nose landing gear 130, and main landing gear 140. The main landing gear 140 of Cottet is configured to provide increased interior space of a fuselage 110, and to extend without hydraulics using gravity and aerodynamic drag. The landing gears 140 include a pair of posts 242 disposed across the fuselage 110. The pair of posts 242 of Cottet generally straddle a center line extending longitudinally along a belly 118 of the fuselage 110. Each post 242 has one or more main wheels 244 rotatably attached thereto. The main landing gear 140 of Cottet includes a truck 410 coupled with the wheels 244, and a shock strut 420 coupled to the truck 410. The main landing gear 140 further includes a trunnion 430 coupled to the bulkhead 370 and configured to pivotally couple the shock strut 420 with the bulkhead 370. The trunnion 430 may comprise a joint structure, such as a shaft rotatably about bearings, to pivotally join the shock strut 420 with the bulkhead 370 or aircraft structure. This is illustrated by Figure 4 of Cottet below:F IG. 4 of Cottet However, Cottet fails to disclose, teach or suggest a second fixation and a third fixation that are connected to each other via a supporting axle, such that the supporting axle is connected to the second fitting and the third fitting in such a manner that the supporting axle forms a main hinge axis.Also, Cottet fails to disclose, teach or suggest a first fixation that forms a hinge axis that is inclined with respect to a main hinge axis.Accordingly, for at least the above reasons, independent claim 1 is patentable over Cottet.Accordingly, for at least the above reasons, independent claim 1 is allowable.Claims 2, 4, 5 and 7-15 all depend either directly or indirectly from claim 1, and are therefore allowable for at least the same reasons as claim 1. Moreover, these claims add further limitations that also render them separately allowable.Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of the rejection of these claims.New Claims New claims 16-22 have been added.As set forth above, claims 7 and 10-15 were indicated as being allowable on page 6 of the Office Action.Without acquiescing in the grounds for rejection, and for expediting prosecution, Applicant has added new claims 16 and 17 based on original claim 1 and allowable claims 14 and 15, respectively; and ii) added new claims 18-22 to depend from independent claims 16 or 17.Accordingly, for at least the above reasons, independent claims 16 and 17 are allowable.Claims 18-22 all depend either directly or indirectly from one of claims 16 or 17, and are therefore allowable for at least the same reasons as claims 16 and 17. Moreover, these claims add further limitations that also render them separately allowable.Conclusion It is believed that all of the stated grounds of rejection have been properly traversed, accommodated, or rendered moot. Applicant therefore respectfully requests that the Patent Office reconsider and withdraw all presently outstanding rejections. It is believed that a full and complete response has been made to the outstanding Office Action and that the present application is in condition for allowance. Thus, prompt and favorable consideration of this amendment is respectfully requested. By addressing particular positions taken by the Patent Office in the above remarks, Applicant does not acquiesce to other positions that have not been explicitly addressed.In addition, Applicant's arguments for the patentability of a claim should not be understood as implying that no other reasons exist for the patentability of that claim.Applicant submits that the claims are in a condition for allowance and respectfully request a notice to that effect. If the Patent Office believes that a discussion or a claim amendment of a minor nature would advance the prosecution of this application, the Patent Office is highly encouraged to telephone the Applicant's attorney at the number given below.Applicant believes no fees to be due in connection with the filing of this paper.However, the Commissioner is hereby authorized to charge any fees or credit any overpayments as a result of the filing of this paper to our Deposit Account No. 02-3978.Respectfully submitted, AXEL FINKBy: /Michael S.
